title: Your flat (Meine Wohnung)
summary: Describe where you live: the rooms, size, light and rent - a classic Munich topic.
goals: Name the rooms of a flat
Describe a flat: groß, klein, hell, dunkel, teuer
Say how many rooms it has
Work out the article of compound nouns

nicosWeg.title: Nicos Weg A1, chapter 6: Living (So wohne ich, Meine Wohnung)

sections.title: Compound nouns: the last part decides
sections.text:
German glues words together into new nouns: [[schlafen]] (to sleep) + [[Zimmer]] = [[das Schlafzimmer]]; [[wohnen]] (to live) + [[Zimmer]] = [[das Wohnzimmer]].

The **last** part decides the article: it is [[das Zimmer]], so it is [[das Schlafzimmer]] and [[das Wohnzimmer]] too. This rule almost never fails, so a long word is often easier than it looks.
Armenian also glues words together (դաս + գիրք = դասագիրք, textbook), so German compounds will feel familiar. Russian more often uses an adjective plus a noun instead.

sections.title: Describing your flat
sections.text:
- [[Meine Wohnung ist klein, aber hell.]]
- [[Die Wohnung hat zwei Zimmer, eine Küche und ein Bad.]]
- [[Die Miete ist sehr hoch.]] (a sentence you will say often in Munich; people also say [[sehr teuer]])

Germans count rooms without the kitchen and the bathroom: a 'Zwei-Zimmer-Wohnung' has two rooms plus a kitchen and a bathroom. The living room counts as a room, like Russian двухкомнатная квартира (unlike English '2-bedroom').

items.question: Which article goes with Wohnzimmer?
items.explanation: The last part decides: das Zimmer, so das Wohnzimmer.

items.prompt: The flat is small but bright.
answers: Die Wohnung ist klein aber hell
items.explanation: Written with a comma: Die Wohnung ist klein, aber hell.
die Miete = the rent; hoch = high (people also say teuer).

items.audio: Die Wohnung hat zwei Zimmer, eine Küche und einen Balkon.
items.question: How many rooms does the flat have?
items.explanation: zwei Zimmer: two rooms, plus a kitchen and a balcony.
